Text:
In the {{c2::diamond}} carry, a patient on a backboard or stretcher is lifted and carried by {{c1::four::number}} providers:

{{c1::one at the head end of the device}}

{{c1::one at the foot end}}

{{c1::one at each side}}
Back Extra:
Cue: the name is the map — the four providers stand at the four points of a diamond: head, foot, and the two sides.

Distinguish: in the one-handed carry, four or more providers each support the backboard with one hand, letting everyone face forward.

Text: A patient on a backboard or stretcher is carried {{c1::feetfirst::headfirst or feetfirst}}.
Back Extra:
Why: feetfirst places the lightest load on the provider at the patient's feet, who must turn around to walk forward.

Why: a conscious patient can also see in the direction of movement, which may reduce anxiety.

Text: When carrying a patient on a backboard or stretcher, the provider at the patient's feet bears the {{c1::lightest::lightest or heaviest}} load — and, to walk forward, turns to grasp the handles with {{c2::back::back or front}} to the device.
Back Extra:
Why: 68–78% of a horizontal patient's body weight is in the torso, so more weight rests on the head half of the device than on the foot half.

Cue: feetfirst deliberately hands the turned-around provider the lightest load.
